note: Open registry. Membership requires only that someone added the record and recorded where it came from. Awards are optional metadata, never a gate. No suitability score lives here.

changelog.change: Normalized MICHELIN tier labels to the program's own verbatim words. The seed migration had copied internal slugs ('recommended', 'bib_gourmand') into the tier field, which is specified to hold the label as published -- 'Selected', 'Bib Gourmand'. Luminosa's compound slug 'green_star+bib_gourmand' was split into TWO award entries, since awards is a list and flattening two recognitions into one label is exactly what the contributor guide forbids.

Correction to the v1.1 session note. The 41-restaurant category harvest was described as needing 'no new code'. That was wrong: src/registry.py gained a harvest_categories parameter on make_record plus a merge branch so the field survives a second sighting. The accurate claim is that no new INGESTION code was needed -- add.py and the batch path were unchanged, and adding a city or a list still requires none. Recorded because an understated diff is how a schema change goes unreviewed.

Added slug aliases after finding that the seed migration silently renamed two records -- 'curate' became 'curate-bar-de-tapas' and 'ukiah' became 'ukiah-japanese-smokehouse', because slugify() ran on the full restaurant name instead of preserving the id the captures were already filed under. Two captured menus (84 dishes) were orphaned and invisible to the app. find() now resolves aliases in both directions, and add_alias() refuses an alias that collides with a different restaurant's live slug.
